summary: Defines the ICMPv6 group of MIB objects, part of the series of IPv6 MIB documents. It lets managers monitor ICMPv6 error and diagnostic messages. It is now historic and was replaced by RFC 4293 and RFC 8096.

eli5.summary: These are counters that count error notes sent on an IPv6 network, so a manager can see how many have gone around.

questions: what is the icmpv6 mib group
what counters does the icmpv6 mib track
subtitle: Counting and monitoring diagnostic messages on IPv6 networks

tldr.problem: IPv6 uses ICMPv6 for error reporting and network diagnostics, such as notifying when a packet is too large to forward or when a destination cannot be reached. Network managers need to monitor these messages.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC defines a MIB group with per-interface counters for each type of ICMPv6 message sent and received, including echo requests, router solicitations, neighbor solicitations, error messages, and multicast group membership messages.
tldr.outcome: Network managers can now monitor ICMPv6 traffic to diagnose network problems and detect network abuse, though this RFC is now historic and replaced by RFC 4293 and RFC 8096.

facts.value: 4: unreachable, time exceeded, parameter problem, packet too big

facts.value: Group membership query, response, and reduction

today: RFC 2466 is Historic. It was replaced by RFC 4293 and RFC 8096, which provide updated MIB definitions for ICMPv6 and IPv6 management using modern SNMP standards.

sections.title: What ICMPv6 Does
sections.content:
ICMPv6 (Internet Control Message Protocol for IPv6) is the way IPv6 devices communicate about problems and ask questions. Unlike ordinary data packets, which carry the actual information an application is sending, ICMP messages carry status information about the network itself.

For example, if a router finds that a packet is too big to send on the next link, it sends an ICMPv6 "Packet Too Big" message back to the sender. If a device wants to discover nearby routers, it sends an ICMPv6 "Router Solicitation" message. These diagnostic and discovery messages are essential to IPv6 operation.
sections.eli5: ICMPv6 is like a feedback channel: when something goes wrong with a delivery, you send a message back to say what happened. When you need information about the network, you ask a question.

sections.title: The ICMPv6 Statistics Table
sections.content:
This RFC defines a single table with per-interface ICMPv6 statistics. For each IPv6 interface on a device, the table tracks counters for messages received and messages sent.

The received side counts how many ICMPv6 messages arrived on the interface, including successful ones and those with errors. The sent side counts how many ICMPv6 messages the interface has transmitted.

Important: a receiving interface is the one to which the message is addressed (where it arrives after routing), which may not be the physical input interface. Similarly, a sending interface is where the message originates, not necessarily where it exits the device.
sections.eli5: The table has one row per interface. For each row, you can see how many messages came in and how many went out.

sections.title: Message Types Counted
sections.content:
The table distinguishes between many ICMPv6 message types:

Error messages report problems: Destination Unreachable (no route exists), Time Exceeded (hop limit reached zero), Parameter Problem (error in the header), and Packet Too Big (packet exceeds path MTU).

Query messages ask questions: Echo Request (like ping), Echo Reply (response to ping), Router Solicitation (asking what routers are here), and Router Advertisement (routers announcing themselves).

Neighbor Discovery messages manage link-local operations: Neighbor Solicitation (asking what physical address matches an IPv6 address, like ARP) and Neighbor Advertisement (answering that question). Redirect messages tell a host a better route exists.

Multicast group membership messages manage multicast (one-to-many) communication: Group Membership Query (asking who is listening), Group Membership Response (saying you are listening), and Group Membership Reduction (saying you are no longer listening).

The table also tracks the total count of messages received and sent, plus error counts for malformed messages.
sections.eli5: There are error messages (something went wrong), questions (do you see routers?), friendship messages (are you my neighbor?), and party messages (is anyone listening to the broadcast?).

sections.title: Using ICMPv6 Statistics for Network Diagnosis
sections.content:
Network managers can use these counters to understand network health. A high count of Time Exceeded messages might indicate that the hop limit is set too low somewhere, or that there is a routing loop. A rising count of Destination Unreachable messages suggests routing problems or configuration errors.

Echo Request and Reply counters show how much ping activity is on the network. Neighbor Solicitation and Advertisement counters indicate normal address discovery traffic. Sudden spikes can reveal network scanning or attacks.

The error counters help detect malformed packets or corrupted ICMP implementations. If one interface consistently shows high error rates while others do not, the problem may be on that interface or the device attached to it.
sections.eli5: Many error messages mean something is broken. Many questions mean devices are looking for routers. Sudden spikes might mean an attacker is probing the network.

sections.title: Security Implications of ICMPv6 Statistics
sections.content:
ICMPv6 statistics reveal how the network is operating, which can be useful for an attacker planning attacks. For example, knowing which devices respond to Router Solicitations tells an attacker where routers are located. Seeing a spike in Destination Unreachable messages might reveal network instability.

Additionally, ICMPv6 messages themselves can be weaponized: a flood of Packet Too Big messages can trigger denial-of-service conditions, and malformed ICMPv6 messages might trigger implementation bugs.

The RFC recommends protecting access to these statistics with SNMPv3 authentication and encryption. Administrators should consider rate-limiting ICMPv6 messages to prevent flooding attacks, while still allowing legitimate diagnostic traffic.
sections.eli5: Knowing what messages are flying around tells attackers what is happening. Fake messages can cause trouble. You need a lock on who can look at these counters.
